description:
Add a --detach flag to mosey launch so the user can background the launcher after it has printed its addresses, without relying on `setsid ... &` plumbing in the shell.

Shape (decided in design pass):

- --detach: standard daemon pattern. Parent re-execs the same binary with MOSEY_DETACHED_FD=3 and SysProcAttr.Setsid=true, child's stdio redirected to /dev/null (or --log-file). Child runs normal startup, writes its address lines to fd 3, closes fd 3, continues. Parent reads from the pipe, mirrors to stderr, exits 0.
- --pidfile=FILE: detached child writes its pid; removes on exit.
- --address-file=FILE: detached child writes its endpoints, one per line; removes on exit.
- --log-file=FILE: where the detached child's logs go (default /dev/null).

UX:

  $ mosey launch --secret=x --detach -- bash
  mosey launch: listening: /ip4/.../p2p/12D3KooW...
  $    # prompt returns; child runs detached

Implementation notes:
- Re-exec via os/exec.Command(os.Args[0], os.Args[1:]...) plus ExtraFiles for the pipe.
- syscall.SysProcAttr{Setsid: true} on darwin+linux. No Windows support needed (mosey is unix-only today).
- Skip the double-fork — Go's runtime doesn't fork() safely, and mosey doesn't open any controlling-tty files in the parent process itself (the child PTY is for the spawned program).
- Bail loudly if --detach is set without an argv (refuse to detach a no-op).
- Cleanup of pidfile/address-file on child exit.
title: mosey launch --detach: daemonize after printing addresses
